item.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=causal-guided+knowledge+editing+foundational+premises+evaluation&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.18653/v1/2026.acl-long.918\", \"title\": [\"CAKE: Causal-Guided Adaptive Knowledge Editing for LLMs\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2026.acl-long.918\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1017/cbo9781139043120.006\", \"title\": [\"Axioms and foundational premises\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1017/cbo9781139043120.006\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2014, 1, 30]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199695300.003.0004\", \"title\": [\"Knowledge, Explanation, and Foundational Premises in Aristotle’s Posterior Analytics\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199695300.003.0004\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2013, 11, 28]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7158698\", \"title\": [\"A Prior-Regularized Framework for Knowledge-Guided Differentiable Causal Discovery\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Purpose: Differentiable causal discovery methods ignore curated domain regulatory knowledge and underperform in high-dimensional, small-sample transcriptomic data. This Methodology paper proposes a universal prior-regularized computational framework that injects pairwise domain priors into gradient-based DAG learning for stable graph recovery in data-limited regimes. Methods: Prior-regularized causal discovery augments the NOTEARS objective with a penalty λ p ∥W-W prior ∥ 2 F , where W prior encodes pairwise interactions from TRRUST and STRING (combined score &gt; 900). The framework supports three backbones (NOTEARS, DAGMA, GOLEM). Validation includes DepMap CRISPR co-essentiality screening (1,208 genes × 18,531 cell lines) and GO enrichment (7,992 cancer-associated genes). Results: On synthetic Erdős-Rényi DAGs across six dimensions (d ∈ {30, 50, 80, 100, 150, 200}) with partial prior coverage (α ∈ {0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7}), prior-regularized NOTEARS improves F1 in 15 of 24 configurations, with 98% relative gain at d = 30 (F1: 0.046 → 0.090) and a mean ∆F1 of 0.014 across all dimensions.
